questions.stem: Which adjustment best fits {patientName}'s later burn-resuscitation record?

answerChoices.label: Reduce the crystalloid infusion and reassess the response
answerChoices.rationale: The urine/perfusion trajectory and rising edema support reducing an excessive infusion rather than continuing a formula as a fixed obligation.

answerChoices.label: Maintain the crystalloid infusion and reassess the response
answerChoices.rationale: Maintaining the escalated rate despite high urine output, stable perfusion and accumulating edema risks ongoing over-resuscitation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Maintaining the escalated rate despite high urine output, stable perfusion and accumulating edema risks ongoing over-resuscitation.

answerChoices.label: Increase the crystalloid infusion and reassess the response
answerChoices.rationale: There is no current oliguria or worsening perfusion to support further fluid escalation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: There is no current oliguria or worsening perfusion to support further fluid escalation.

questions.explanation: The response now matters more than the initial arithmetic. High urine output with stable perfusion and increasing edema supports reducing the crystalloid rate with reassessment. This does not teach a universal percentage change or an electrical-injury urine target.

questions.stem: Which decompression plan best fits {patientName}'s right forearm at this point in the outside record?

answerChoices.label: Perform forearm escharotomy and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: The regional deterioration under a circumferential deep thermal burn persists despite simple external measures and adequate systemic perfusion, supporting release through constrictive eschar.

answerChoices.label: Perform forearm fasciotomy and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: A deeper compartment operation is not the first supported release for this skin-envelope pattern without evidence of muscle injury; reassess after adequate eschar release.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A deeper compartment operation is not the first supported release for this skin-envelope pattern without evidence of muscle injury; reassess after adequate eschar release.

answerChoices.label: Continue forearm elevation and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: The perfusion trajectory worsens despite elevation and removal of external constriction, so continued observation alone does not resolve the mechanical problem.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The perfusion trajectory worsens despite elevation and removal of external constriction, so continued observation alone does not resolve the mechanical problem.

questions.explanation: Local deterioration with stable systemic and opposite-hand perfusion points to the circumferential thermal envelope. Release constrictive eschar, then reassess. Fasciotomy addresses a deeper compartment problem and may be necessary if that problem is demonstrated or perfusion fails to recover after adequate skin release.

questions.stem: Which immediate procedure best fits {patientName}'s later ventilatory findings in the outside hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Thoracic escharotomy
answerChoices.rationale: The pressure pattern and restricted excursion localize a compliance problem to the circumferential burned chest wall after the represented tube and pleural checks.

answerChoices.label: Endotracheal tube exchange
answerChoices.rationale: An isolated tube obstruction is less consistent with a freely passing catheter and increased plateau as well as peak pressure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An isolated tube obstruction is less consistent with a freely passing catheter and increased plateau as well as peak pressure.

answerChoices.label: Tube thoracostomy
answerChoices.rationale: The symmetric examination and represented pleural sliding do not support a pneumothorax as the cause of the marked external restriction.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The symmetric examination and represented pleural sliding do not support a pneumothorax as the cause of the marked external restriction.

questions.explanation: Infer reduced chest compliance from the combined pressures and excursion. Then integrate the tube and pleural checks with the circumferential deep chest wound to select thoracic escharotomy. This is a historical hospital procedure review, not a procedure performed in the founder's clinic.

questions.stem: Which fluid plan best fits {patientName}'s first hospital review after the electrical injury?

answerChoices.label: Increase crystalloid with renal and electrolyte monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: The muscle and pigment findings indicate a resuscitation problem that is not represented by the small cutaneous TBSA. Carefully increase and titrate fluid while monitoring renal response and electrolytes.

answerChoices.label: Maintain crystalloid with renal and electrolyte monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: The current maintenance regimen is accompanied by falling output and rising creatinine in pigment-producing muscle injury.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The current maintenance regimen is accompanied by falling output and rising creatinine in pigment-producing muscle injury.

answerChoices.label: Reduce crystalloid with renal and electrolyte monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Swelling alone does not justify restriction while the represented pigment injury and renal response suggest inadequate current delivery. Reassess volume status rather than interpreting all edema as overload.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Swelling alone does not justify restriction while the represented pigment injury and renal response suggest inadequate current delivery. Reassess volume status rather than interpreting all edema as overload.

questions.explanation: A small entry/exit area can conceal substantial muscle injury. The CK, myoglobin and renal trajectory support increased monitored crystalloid rather than relying on skin TBSA. Reassess to avoid both inadequate perfusion and fluid excess; this item sets no universal electrical-injury output target.

questions.stem: Which procedure best fits {patientName}'s later forearm findings in the outside hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Forearm compartment fasciotomy
answerChoices.rationale: Progressive deep-compartment findings after electrical muscle injury require fascial release; preserved arterial signals do not make the deep tissue pressure problem disappear.

answerChoices.label: Forearm skin escharotomy
answerChoices.rationale: There is no constricting circumferential skin envelope to release, and skin incision would not decompress the affected deep compartments.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: There is no constricting circumferential skin envelope to release, and skin incision would not decompress the affected deep compartments.

answerChoices.label: Forearm arterial thrombectomy
answerChoices.rationale: The deep tension and stretch-pain trajectory with maintained arterial signals points to compartment pressure rather than a demonstrated arterial occlusion.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The deep tension and stretch-pain trajectory with maintained arterial signals points to compartment pressure rather than a demonstrated arterial occlusion.

questions.explanation: Integrate the deep pain/tension trajectory with the electrical mechanism and pliable skin. The threatened compartment lies beneath fascia, so skin eschar release does not address it. Maintained Doppler signals cannot by themselves exclude a deep compartment syndrome.

questions.stem: Which additional blood investigation best addresses {patientName}'s persistent findings after smoke exposure in the initial outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Blood co-oximetry
answerChoices.rationale: COHb can impair oxygen carriage despite a reassuring conventional saturation and high dissolved oxygen tension. Blood co-oximetry directly measures the relevant hemoglobin species.

answerChoices.label: Repeat arterial oxygen tension
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating dissolved oxygen measurement does not establish whether hemoglobin is carrying CO.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Repeating dissolved oxygen measurement does not establish whether hemoglobin is carrying CO.

answerChoices.label: Blood hemoglobin concentration
answerChoices.rationale: Carrier quantity does not measure how much is occupied by CO. It does not resolve this exposure-related discrepancy.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Carrier quantity does not measure how much is occupied by CO. It does not resolve this exposure-related discrepancy.

questions.explanation: Separate dissolved oxygen and conventional saturation from functional hemoglobin carriage. A normal reading does not exclude CO exposure. Add blood co-oximetry while emergency clinicians continue appropriate treatment and reassessment.

questions.stem: Which additional care plan best fits {patientName}'s later outside-hospital assessment?

answerChoices.label: Seek urgent hyperbaric-medicine consultation
answerChoices.rationale: The newly documented loss of consciousness and acquired neurologic deficits remain important despite a lower COHb after treatment. Consultation should consider HBO in the complete clinical setting.

answerChoices.label: Continue monitored hospital care without hyperbaric consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Monitored oxygen is already shared background care. With these neurologic features, omitting specialist consideration on the basis of the low treated level underestimates severity.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Monitored oxygen is already shared background care. With these neurologic features, omitting specialist consideration on the basis of the low treated level underestimates severity.

answerChoices.label: Arrange discharge with scheduled neurologic follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent deficits and documented loss of consciousness do not fit a routine discharge decision at this assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Persistent deficits and documented loss of consciousness do not fit a routine discharge decision at this assessment.

questions.explanation: A treated COHb is not the complete severity record. Prior unconsciousness and persistent cognitive deficits warrant urgent hyperbaric consultation while current oxygen and monitoring continue. The item keys specialist consideration, not guaranteed benefit or mandatory HBO for every elevated COHb.

questions.stem: Which airway plan best fits {patientName}'s changing findings before the outside-hospital transfer?

answerChoices.label: Secure the airway by endotracheal intubation before transfer
answerChoices.rationale: Progressive voice, secretion and inspiratory changes indicate a threatened upper airway despite preserved saturation; diagnostic work should not delay airway control.

answerChoices.label: Give nebulized bronchodilator treatment before transfer
answerChoices.rationale: The progressive voice and secretion changes with inspiratory noise indicate an upper-airway threat; a lower-airway bronchodilator does not secure that airway.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The progressive voice and secretion changes with inspiratory noise indicate an upper-airway threat; a lower-airway bronchodilator does not secure that airway.

answerChoices.label: Continue oxygen and reassess the airway during transfer
answerChoices.rationale: Oxygen and a reassuring saturation do not prevent mechanical airway obstruction from progressing en route.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Oxygen and a reassuring saturation do not prevent mechanical airway obstruction from progressing en route.

questions.explanation: The serial findings concern upper-airway patency, not simply oxygen delivery. Secure that airway before transfer rather than wait for hypoxemia or rely on a lower-airway bronchodilator. Facial soot by itself would not establish this same indication.

questions.stem: Which investigation best addresses {patientName}'s lower-airway assessment in the later burn-unit record?

answerChoices.label: Flexible bronchoscopy
answerChoices.rationale: Direct examination can establish and grade lower-airway mucosal injury and assess retained airway debris after stabilization.

answerChoices.label: Chest computed tomography
answerChoices.rationale: CT can assess thoracic and parenchymal disease, but the specified unresolved question is mucosal distribution and debris within the airway.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: CT can assess thoracic and parenchymal disease, but the specified unresolved question is mucosal distribution and debris within the airway.

answerChoices.label: Repeat chest radiography
answerChoices.rationale: A later radiograph can track pulmonary changes but does not directly grade the airway surface or inspect retained debris.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A later radiograph can track pulmonary changes but does not directly grade the airway surface or inspect retained debris.

questions.explanation: Match the unresolved anatomy to the investigation. After stabilization, direct lower-airway examination can assess the mucosa and debris even when an early chest radiograph is unrevealing. Imaging still has other roles; the key does not declare CT or radiographs useless.

questions.stem: Which antidote plan best fits {patientName}'s recorded hospital condition while supportive treatment continues?

answerChoices.label: Administer intravenous hydroxocobalamin now
answerChoices.rationale: The exposure, coma/collapse and profound persistent lactate support empiric treatment for suspected cyanide toxicity. Hydroxocobalamin avoids adding the nitrite-associated methemoglobin burden to documented CO exposure.

answerChoices.label: Administer sodium nitrite with thiosulfate now
answerChoices.rationale: This is a genuine cyanide regimen, but sodium nitrite can worsen hypotension and oxygen carriage through methemoglobin formation when CO poisoning coexists. The preferred available alternative here is hydroxocobalamin.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is a genuine cyanide regimen, but sodium nitrite can worsen hypotension and oxygen carriage through methemoglobin formation when CO poisoning coexists. The preferred available alternative here is hydroxocobalamin.

answerChoices.label: Await the blood cyanide result before antidote treatment
answerChoices.rationale: A reference-laboratory result should not defer treatment when severe exposure and clinical findings make suspicion high.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A reference-laboratory result should not defer treatment when severe exposure and clinical findings make suspicion high.

questions.explanation: Infer possible cyanide toxicity in addition to the measured CO exposure, then account for the oxygen-carriage and hypotension risks of sodium nitrite when choosing treatment. The history and collapse justify empiric hydroxocobalamin without waiting for a send-out result. Lactate here is a constructed observation, not a universal diagnostic cutoff.

questions.stem: Which calcium treatment route best fits {patientName}'s later findings in the outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Intravenous calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Bilateral neuromuscular findings, ECG changes and falling serum calcium indicate systemic toxicity; intravenous replacement with surveillance addresses the systemic deficit.

answerChoices.label: Topical calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Topical treatment targets the exposed skin, but local improvement does not correct the documented systemic calcium deficit and cardiac manifestations.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Topical treatment targets the exposed skin, but local improvement does not correct the documented systemic calcium deficit and cardiac manifestations.

answerChoices.label: Local calcium gluconate infiltration
answerChoices.rationale: Local infiltration may be considered for selected persistent local injury, but it does not replace systemic treatment for this acquired multisystem pattern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Local infiltration may be considered for selected persistent local injury, but it does not replace systemic treatment for this acquired multisystem pattern.

questions.explanation: Reduced local pain is not proof that absorbed fluoride is harmless. Interpret the distant spasms, ECG course and serum calcium together, then use the systemic route under monitoring. No injection concentration, dose or intra-arterial technique is prescribed in this draft.

questions.stem: Which regional wound plan best fits {patientName}'s recorded trunk examination when planning burn excision and coverage?

answerChoices.label: Plan excision and coverage of the central region
answerChoices.rationale: The central pattern indicates deeper nonviable tissue, while the advancing peripheral epithelialization supports preserving that region rather than treating the field as uniform.

answerChoices.label: Plan excision and coverage of the entire wound
answerChoices.rationale: Uniform excision would remove the represented viable epithelializing periphery along with the deeper center.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Uniform excision would remove the represented viable epithelializing periphery along with the deeper center.

answerChoices.label: Plan continued dressing care for the entire wound
answerChoices.rationale: Peripheral healing does not establish that the dry insensate center will close by the same pathway.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Peripheral healing does not establish that the dry insensate center will close by the same pathway.

questions.explanation: Infer regional tissue viability, then use it to set the surgical field. The central deeper region needs burn-surgical excision/coverage planning; the viable healing edge should not be excised merely because it belongs to the same wound. No exact operation date or graft area is prescribed.

questions.stem: Which coverage plan best fits {patientName}'s later operative record?

answerChoices.label: Apply cadaveric allograft over the excised bed
answerChoices.rationale: An excised viable bed needs coverage while current donor regions recover; allograft supplies temporary coverage without treating it as definitive autologous skin.

answerChoices.label: Reharvest the open donor regions for autograft
answerChoices.rationale: The represented donor wounds have not healed; treating them as immediately reusable ignores the operative record and adds donor injury.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The represented donor wounds have not healed; treating them as immediately reusable ignores the operative record and adds donor injury.

answerChoices.label: Maintain topical dressings over the excised bed
answerChoices.rationale: Simple dressing care does not provide the same temporary biologic coverage for this broad excised bed when a staged coverage pathway is required.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Simple dressing care does not provide the same temporary biologic coverage for this broad excised bed when a staged coverage pathway is required.

questions.explanation: The bed has been prepared, but current autograft donor regions are still healing. Temporary cadaveric coverage can bridge that interval during staged major-burn care. It is not permanent autologous coverage, and no fixed replacement date is inferred.

questions.stem: Which initial nutrition plan best fits {patientName}'s first outside burn-unit assessment?

answerChoices.label: Start low-rate gastric enteral nutrition
answerChoices.rationale: The acquired perfusion and abdominal record supports a cautious enteral start. Quiet bowel sounds alone do not establish bowel ischemia or obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Start primary parenteral nutrition
answerChoices.rationale: The record supplies no established reason that the gut route is unusable; a quiet examination alone does not make PN the preferred initial route.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record supplies no established reason that the gut route is unusable; a quiet examination alone does not make PN the preferred initial route.

answerChoices.label: Defer nutrition until stool passage
answerChoices.rationale: Waiting for stool adds a prerequisite not supported by the represented perfusion recovery and abdominal findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Waiting for stool adds a prerequisite not supported by the represented perfusion recovery and abdominal findings.

questions.explanation: Interpret the current resuscitation trajectory and abdominal findings together. They support a cautious enteral start despite quiet bowel sounds. This question does not prescribe an exact hour, calorie target, access procedure or advancement schedule.

questions.stem: Which feeding prescription best fits {patientName}'s later outside-hospital findings while the abdominal assessment proceeds?

answerChoices.label: Pause enteral delivery during reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The new hypoperfusion and abdominal warnings differ from the earlier feeding-eligible state. Changing access does not restore intestinal perfusion.

answerChoices.label: Continue low-rate gastric enteral delivery
answerChoices.rationale: A low-rate prescription is not sufficient reassurance when support and abdominal findings now raise concern for compromised intestinal safety.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A low-rate prescription is not sufficient reassurance when support and abdominal findings now raise concern for compromised intestinal safety.

answerChoices.label: Change to low-rate postpyloric enteral delivery
answerChoices.rationale: A postpyloric route can address selected gastric delivery problems but does not bypass hypoperfused bowel or suspected ischemia.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A postpyloric route can address selected gastric delivery problems but does not bypass hypoperfused bowel or suspected ischemia.

questions.explanation: The earlier feeding decision does not remain valid automatically. Interpret the new support/perfusion course and changed abdomen, then pause enteral delivery during urgent assessment. Moving the tube beyond the stomach is not a treatment for compromised bowel perfusion; immediate PN is not inferred.

questions.stem: Which antimicrobial plan best fits {patientName}'s wound at this clinic review?

answerChoices.label: Continue the current antimicrobial dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: The healing trajectory and unchanged surrounding skin do not establish infection requiring systemic treatment. Interpret surface growth with the examination and continue reassessment.

answerChoices.label: Add oral ciprofloxacin to the dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: Susceptibility states what might treat the organism if systemic therapy were indicated; it does not itself establish that this improving wound requires an antibiotic course.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Susceptibility states what might treat the organism if systemic therapy were indicated; it does not itself establish that this improving wound requires an antibiotic course.

answerChoices.label: Add intravenous cefepime to the dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: A susceptible surface organism does not establish deep invasive disease or a need for intravenous therapy in this healing, clinically well patient.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A susceptible surface organism does not establish deep invasive disease or a need for intravenous therapy in this healing, clinically well patient.

questions.explanation: First interpret the surface specimen alongside actual wound behavior. Then decide whether systemic therapy is indicated. Healing and an unchanged surrounding examination favor local care; a susceptibility report is not a prescription by itself. New tissue deterioration, spreading inflammation or systemic illness would require reassessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which disposition best fits {patientName}'s scald at this clinic review?

answerChoices.label: Burn-service consultation with local wound follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The dermal component is small, with preserved blanching and manageable wound care. The larger intact erythematous area does not establish a large dermal burn requiring transfer.

answerChoices.label: Burn-service consultation with inpatient burn admission
answerChoices.rationale: Counting every red area as dermal injury exaggerates severity. Current depth, function and care requirements do not establish a need for inpatient admission.

answerChoices.label: Burn-service consultation with emergency hospital transfer
answerChoices.rationale: There is no physiologic or limb-threatening feature in the recorded course to justify emergency retrieval over planned ambulatory co-management.

decisionNodes.explanation: First separate dermal injury from epidermal erythema. Then match the actual wound and care needs to an outpatient pathway. Consultation can help local management; it does not make every scald an inpatient transfer.

answerChoices.label: Arrange prompt assessment by the burn surgical service
answerChoices.rationale: The depth pattern and joint involvement need specialist planning even though distal circulation is maintained.

answerChoices.label: Arrange continued dressings through the general clinic
answerChoices.rationale: A small surface area does not remove the functional and depth concern over hand joints.

answerChoices.label: Arrange emergency assessment by the vascular surgical service
answerChoices.rationale: Reduced wound sensation can reflect depth; the recorded distal perfusion does not support an arterial emergency as the primary referral target.

decisionNodes.stem: Using the outside hospital's stated worksheet, which starting infusion rate should have been recorded for {patientName} at arrival, rounded to the nearest whole mL/hour?

answerChoices.label: Crystalloid at 378 mL/hour
answerChoices.rationale: Count 14% plus 8%, giving 22%. The first allocation is 3 × 70 × 22 / 2 = 2310 mL. Subtract 800 mL, then divide the remaining 1510 mL by the four hours remaining: 377.5 mL/hour.

answerChoices.label: Crystalloid at 693 mL/hour
answerChoices.rationale: This result counts the additional epidermal erythema: (3 × 70 × 34 / 2 − 800) / 4 = 692.5. The intact red region does not belong in this dermal-burn estimate.

answerChoices.label: Crystalloid at 189 mL/hour
answerChoices.rationale: This result restarts an eight-hour window at arrival: (2310 − 800) / 8 = 188.75. The supplied worksheet measures time from the injury.

decisionNodes.explanation: The dermal-burn total is 22%, not the 34% of visibly changed skin. The worksheet's first allocation is 2310 mL; 1510 mL remains after transport fluid. Four hours remain in its injury-based window, giving 377.5, rounded to 378 mL/hour. This calculation applies only to the specified worksheet.

decisionNodes.stem: Which decompression plan best fits {patientName}'s right forearm at this point in the outside record?

answerChoices.label: Perform forearm escharotomy and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: The regional deterioration under a circumferential deep thermal burn persists despite simple external measures and adequate systemic perfusion, supporting release through constrictive eschar.

answerChoices.label: Perform forearm fasciotomy and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: A deeper compartment operation is not the first supported release for this skin-envelope pattern without evidence of muscle injury; reassess after adequate eschar release.

answerChoices.label: Continue forearm elevation and reassess distal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: The perfusion trajectory worsens despite elevation and removal of external constriction, so continued observation alone does not resolve the mechanical problem.

decisionNodes.explanation: Local deterioration with stable systemic and opposite-hand perfusion points to the circumferential thermal envelope. Release constrictive eschar, then reassess. decisionNodes.stem: Which additional blood investigation best addresses {patientName}'s persistent findings after smoke exposure in the initial outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Blood co-oximetry
answerChoices.rationale: COHb can impair oxygen carriage despite a reassuring conventional saturation and high dissolved oxygen tension. Blood co-oximetry directly measures the relevant hemoglobin species.

answerChoices.label: Repeat arterial oxygen tension
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating dissolved oxygen measurement does not establish whether hemoglobin is carrying CO.

answerChoices.label: Blood hemoglobin concentration
answerChoices.rationale: Carrier quantity does not measure how much is occupied by CO. It does not resolve this exposure-related discrepancy.

decisionNodes.explanation: Separate dissolved oxygen and conventional saturation from functional hemoglobin carriage. A normal reading does not exclude CO exposure. Add blood co-oximetry while emergency clinicians continue appropriate treatment and reassessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which additional care plan best fits {patientName}'s later outside-hospital assessment?

answerChoices.label: Seek urgent hyperbaric-medicine consultation
answerChoices.rationale: The newly documented loss of consciousness and acquired neurologic deficits remain important despite a lower COHb after treatment. Consultation should consider HBO in the complete clinical setting.

answerChoices.label: Continue monitored hospital care without hyperbaric consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Monitored oxygen is already shared background care. With these neurologic features, omitting specialist consideration on the basis of the low treated level underestimates severity.

answerChoices.label: Arrange discharge with scheduled neurologic follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent deficits and documented loss of consciousness do not fit a routine discharge decision at this assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which airway plan best fits {patientName}'s changing findings before the outside-hospital transfer?

answerChoices.label: Secure the airway by endotracheal intubation before transfer

answerChoices.label: Give nebulized bronchodilator treatment before transfer

answerChoices.rationale: Oxygen and a reassuring saturation do not prevent mechanical airway obstruction from progressing en route.

decisionNodes.stem: Which antidote plan best fits {patientName}'s recorded hospital condition while supportive treatment continues?

answerChoices.label: Administer intravenous hydroxocobalamin now
answerChoices.rationale: The exposure, coma/collapse and profound persistent lactate support empiric treatment for suspected cyanide toxicity. Hydroxocobalamin avoids adding the nitrite-associated methemoglobin burden to documented CO exposure.

answerChoices.label: Administer sodium nitrite with thiosulfate now
answerChoices.rationale: This is a genuine cyanide regimen, but sodium nitrite can worsen hypotension and oxygen carriage through methemoglobin formation when CO poisoning coexists. The preferred available alternative here is hydroxocobalamin.

answerChoices.label: Await the blood cyanide result before antidote treatment
answerChoices.rationale: A reference-laboratory result should not defer treatment when severe exposure and clinical findings make suspicion high.

decisionNodes.explanation: Infer possible cyanide toxicity in addition to the measured CO exposure, then account for the oxygen-carriage and hypotension risks of sodium nitrite when choosing treatment. The history and collapse justify empiric hydroxocobalamin without waiting for a send-out result. Lactate here is a constructed observation, not a universal diagnostic cutoff.

decisionNodes.stem: Which calcium treatment route best fits {patientName}'s later findings in the outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Intravenous calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Bilateral neuromuscular findings, ECG changes and falling serum calcium indicate systemic toxicity; intravenous replacement with surveillance addresses the systemic deficit.

answerChoices.label: Topical calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Topical treatment targets the exposed skin, but local improvement does not correct the documented systemic calcium deficit and cardiac manifestations.

answerChoices.label: Local calcium gluconate infiltration
answerChoices.rationale: Local infiltration may be considered for selected persistent local injury, but it does not replace systemic treatment for this acquired multisystem pattern.

decisionNodes.explanation: Reduced local pain is not proof that absorbed fluoride is harmless. Interpret the distant spasms, ECG course and serum calcium together, then use the systemic route under monitoring. No injection concentration, dose or intra-arterial technique is prescribed in this draft.

decisionNodes.stem: Which regional wound plan best fits {patientName}'s recorded trunk examination when planning burn excision and coverage?

answerChoices.label: Plan excision and coverage of the central region
answerChoices.rationale: The central pattern indicates deeper nonviable tissue, while the advancing peripheral epithelialization supports preserving that region rather than treating the field as uniform.

answerChoices.label: Plan excision and coverage of the entire wound
answerChoices.rationale: Uniform excision would remove the represented viable epithelializing periphery along with the deeper center.

answerChoices.label: Plan continued dressing care for the entire wound
answerChoices.rationale: Peripheral healing does not establish that the dry insensate center will close by the same pathway.

decisionNodes.explanation: Infer regional tissue viability, then use it to set the surgical field. The central deeper region needs burn-surgical excision/coverage planning; the viable healing edge should not be excised merely because it belongs to the same wound. No exact operation date or graft area is prescribed.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: During a later operation, a broad excised trunk bed shows viable bleeding tissue and no residual eschar. The unburned thighs and back have already been harvested in earlier stages and remain open donor wounds. Other deep burns are still undergoing staged excision. The team must cover the current bed while those donor regions recover.
decisionNodes.stem: Which coverage plan best fits {patientName}'s later operative record?

answerChoices.label: Apply cadaveric allograft over the excised bed
answerChoices.rationale: An excised viable bed needs coverage while current donor regions recover; allograft supplies temporary coverage without treating it as definitive autologous skin.

answerChoices.label: Reharvest the open donor regions for autograft
answerChoices.rationale: The represented donor wounds have not healed; treating them as immediately reusable ignores the operative record and adds donor injury.

answerChoices.label: Maintain topical dressings over the excised bed
answerChoices.rationale: Simple dressing care does not provide the same temporary biologic coverage for this broad excised bed when a staged coverage pathway is required.

decisionNodes.explanation: The bed has been prepared, but current autograft donor regions are still healing. Temporary cadaveric coverage can bridge that interval during staged major-burn care. It is not permanent autologous coverage, and no fixed replacement date is inferred.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial nutrition plan best fits {patientName}'s first outside burn-unit assessment?

answerChoices.label: Start low-rate gastric enteral nutrition
answerChoices.rationale: The acquired perfusion and abdominal record supports a cautious enteral start. Quiet bowel sounds alone do not establish bowel ischemia or obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Start primary parenteral nutrition
answerChoices.rationale: The record supplies no established reason that the gut route is unusable; a quiet examination alone does not make PN the preferred initial route.

answerChoices.label: Defer nutrition until stool passage
answerChoices.rationale: Waiting for stool adds a prerequisite not supported by the represented perfusion recovery and abdominal findings.

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret the current resuscitation trajectory and abdominal findings together. They support a cautious enteral start despite quiet bowel sounds. This question does not prescribe an exact hour, calorie target, access procedure or advancement schedule.
sourceLabels: Foundations of burn patient care, December 2025
ESICM early enteral nutrition guideline, 2017

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Later, the record shows that gastric feeding had been tolerated. Vasopressor support is then restarted and increased, urine output falls and lactate rises. The abdomen becomes distended and tender, and blood appears in gastric drainage. Urgent resuscitation and abdominal assessment proceed.
decisionNodes.stem: Which feeding prescription best fits {patientName}'s later outside-hospital findings while the abdominal assessment proceeds?

answerChoices.label: Pause enteral delivery during reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The new hypoperfusion and abdominal warnings differ from the earlier feeding-eligible state. Changing access does not restore intestinal perfusion.

answerChoices.label: Continue low-rate gastric enteral delivery
answerChoices.rationale: A low-rate prescription is not sufficient reassurance when support and abdominal findings now raise concern for compromised intestinal safety.

answerChoices.label: Change to low-rate postpyloric enteral delivery
answerChoices.rationale: A postpyloric route can address selected gastric delivery problems but does not bypass hypoperfused bowel or suspected ischemia.

decisionNodes.explanation: The earlier feeding decision does not remain valid automatically. Interpret the new support/perfusion course and changed abdomen, then pause enteral delivery during urgent assessment. Moving the tube beyond the stomach is not a treatment for compromised bowel perfusion; immediate PN is not inferred.

decisionNodes.stem: Which antimicrobial plan best fits {patientName}'s wound at this clinic review?

answerChoices.label: Continue the current antimicrobial dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: The healing trajectory and unchanged surrounding skin do not establish infection requiring systemic treatment. Interpret surface growth with the examination and continue reassessment.

answerChoices.label: Add oral ciprofloxacin to the dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: Susceptibility states what might treat the organism if systemic therapy were indicated; it does not itself establish that this improving wound requires an antibiotic course.

answerChoices.label: Add intravenous cefepime to the dressing regimen
answerChoices.rationale: A susceptible surface organism does not establish deep invasive disease or a need for intravenous therapy in this healing, clinically well patient.

decisionNodes.explanation: First interpret the surface specimen alongside actual wound behavior. Then decide whether systemic therapy is indicated. Healing and an unchanged surrounding examination favor local care; a susceptibility report is not a prescription by itself. New tissue deterioration, spreading inflammation or systemic illness would require reassessment.

review.title: Investigate reassuring oxygen readings after a fire

cues.phrase: Repeat arterial oxygen tension
cues.why: The stem already reports a high arterial oxygen tension. Repeating the same measurement is a weak foil without a new acquisition or clinical reason.

cues.phrase: Blood co-oximetry
cues.why: The shared 'ox' language with repeated oxygen readings is not sufficient by itself to reveal the key, but the key is also the only novel oxygen-related blood test; the other novel option measures hemoglobin amount.

fairness: Blood co-oximetry is the best offered investigation for suspected CO exposure despite reassuring conventional oxygen measurements. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The task is clear, but it tests the classic fire-plus-reassuring-saturation test association. Rejecting repetition of an already reassuring PaO2 is not a second consequential step.
The initial node is coherent with a later CO severity decision. Its explanation names CO but does not prescribe hyperbaric consultation, so it does not directly give away the later management key.
suggestions: Replace the disposable repeat-test foil with a credible investigation addressing a genuine competing explanation of the patient's observations.

To reach the requested level, test what discordant observed measurements establish and how that changes a concrete next decision; alternatively seek explicit acceptance as foundational CO test recognition.

question.stem: Which additional blood investigation best addresses {patientName}'s persistent findings after smoke exposure in the initial outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Blood co-oximetry
answerChoices.rationale: A high arterial oxygen tension and conventional pulse saturation do not exclude impaired oxygen carriage from CO; co-oximetry measures COHb.

answerChoices.label: Blood lactate concentration
answerChoices.rationale: Lactate can help assess smoke-related systemic toxicity or poor perfusion but does not determine the carboxyhemoglobin fraction responsible for this diagnostic discordance.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Lactate can help assess smoke-related systemic toxicity or poor perfusion but does not determine the carboxyhemoglobin fraction responsible for this diagnostic discordance.

answerChoices.label: Blood hemoglobin concentration
answerChoices.rationale: Hemoglobin concentration does not quantify the fraction bound to CO. A concentration result cannot replace the indicated dyshemoglobin measurement.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Hemoglobin concentration does not quantify the fraction bound to CO. A concentration result cannot replace the indicated dyshemoglobin measurement.

question.explanation: Normal conventional saturation and high arterial oxygen tension do not exclude CO poisoning. Blood co-oximetry provides a COHb measurement; clinical interpretation must account for oxygen and elapsed time.

review.title: Secure a deteriorating smoke-exposed airway

cues.phrase: saliva pools because swallowing is difficult, and inspiratory noise appears
cues.why: The combination makes threatened airway patency unmistakable; waiting during transfer or giving a bronchodilator are not close alternatives.

cues.phrase: Which airway plan
cues.why: 'Secure the airway' in the key closely echoes the task, although the overlap alone is not the main problem. The other choices do not provide comparable airway control.

fairness: Intubation before transfer is clearly the best offered plan. The warning signs must remain; a normal oxygen saturation does not justify waiting. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

This is urgent airway recognition followed by the standard response, with no second consequential decision among credible competitors. It duplicates much of the emergency-disposition item's safety lesson.
The sequence is coherent: later intubation and transfer are consistent with this decision. The first explanation does not explicitly name the later bronchoscopy answer.
suggestions: Seek explicit acceptance as an easy safety item or merge its purpose with the smoke-transfer item. If retaining a routine resident reasoning objective, compare clinically credible airway/stabilization sequences with supported decision-critical observations.
Do not make it harder by removing signs of impending obstruction or adding delay to a clearly indicated airway intervention.

answerChoices.rationale: Deferring airway control to the receiving unit is unsafe with the represented progressive voice, swallowing and inspiratory findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Deferring airway control to the receiving unit is unsafe with the represented progressive voice, swallowing and inspiratory findings.

answerChoices.rationale: Chest imaging does not resolve the current upper-airway patency problem and should not delay airway management.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Chest imaging does not resolve the current upper-airway patency problem and should not delay airway management.

caseDefinition.presentation: {patientName}, a 58-year-old man, reviews his outside hospital admission with the founder in clinic after an enclosed workshop fire. At the first recorded assessment he had soot around his mouth and could speak in full sentences. The hospital then documented the serial observations below.

nodes.displayName: Secure a deteriorating smoke-exposed airway
nodes.learningObjective: Interpret an evolving upper-airway trajectory and choose airway control rather than bronchodilator treatment or oxygen observation before transfer.
nodes.currentUpdate: His voice becomes faint and coarse, saliva pools because swallowing is difficult, and inspiratory noise appears. He remains awake and finger oxygen saturation is 97% on oxygen. The outside team is preparing transfer to a burn unit.
nodes.stem: Which immediate sequence is indicated before {patientName}'s transfer in the outside-hospital record?

options.label: Endotracheal intubation, followed by burn-unit transfer
options.rationale: The progressive obstructive findings require airway control before transport; normal conventional saturation does not establish patency.
options.temptation: Prioritize the changing airway before transport.
options.whenReasonable: This progression supports airway control before the transfer.

options.label: Burn-unit transfer, followed by endotracheal intubation
options.rationale: Deferring airway control to the receiving unit is unsafe with the represented progressive voice, swallowing and inspiratory findings.
options.temptation: Move first to definitive burn expertise despite current airway deterioration.
options.whenReasonable: A stable patent airway without progressive warning signs could permit transfer without pre-transfer intubation.

options.label: Chest radiography, followed by burn-unit transfer
options.rationale: Chest imaging does not resolve the current upper-airway patency problem and should not delay airway management.
options.temptation: Seek an initial diagnostic study before acting on the airway examination.
options.whenReasonable: After airway stabilization, chest imaging can investigate pulmonary or thoracic findings.

nodes.explanation: The changing voice, secretion handling and inspiratory noise indicate a threatened airway. Stabilize it before transport or nonessential investigation; a reassuring conventional saturation does not negate those observations.

review.title: Treat systemic toxicity after an HF burn

cues.phrase: hand spasms on both sides and ventricular ectopy
cues.why: These distant manifestations plus an explicitly low serum calcium make systemic treatment the obvious route; the two localized routes have little remaining plausibility.

cues.phrase: Which calcium treatment route
cues.why: The task supplies the treatment and asks only for its route. Intravenous is the sole systemic option beside two local therapies.

fairness: Intravenous calcium gluconate under monitoring is the best offered route for the described systemic manifestations. Reduced local pain does not establish resolution of systemic toxicity. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

Because the low calcium and named treatment are already supplied, the item is principally systemic-versus-local route recognition. The initial local response does not create a difficult second decision once ventricular ectopy and hypocalcemia are given.
Standalone chronology and task are clear. HF systemic toxicity is a worthwhile chemical-burn teaching point, although this review makes no claim about measured exam frequency.
suggestions: Retain the local-versus-systemic distinction and urgent findings. Seek acceptance as focused safety recognition, or test a supported next decision among credible systemic management plans rather than three routes with only one systemic choice.
Do not add unsourced doses, injection concentrations or specialist techniques to manufacture difficulty.

question.stem: Which immediate treatment best addresses {patientName}'s acquired findings in the outside-hospital record?

answerChoices.label: Intravenous calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Bilateral spasm, ectopy, QT lengthening and low serum calcium establish a systemic treatment need beyond the improved local pain.

answerChoices.label: Topical calcium gluconate
answerChoices.rationale: Topical treatment addresses the skin exposure but does not treat the represented systemic calcium disturbance.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Topical treatment addresses the skin exposure but does not treat the represented systemic calcium disturbance.

answerChoices.label: Local calcium gluconate infiltration
answerChoices.rationale: A local delivery technique is not the systemic treatment indicated by distant neuromuscular and cardiac effects; its agent-specific technique is not prescribed here.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A local delivery technique is not the systemic treatment indicated by distant neuromuscular and cardiac effects; its agent-specific technique is not prescribed here.

question.explanation: The acquired distant neuromuscular and cardiac findings with low calcium indicate systemic fluoride toxicity. Intravenous calcium is assessed under ECG and electrolyte surveillance with toxicology guidance; no dose, concentration or local injection technique is taught.

clinicalCase.presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old man, reviews his outside hospital record in clinic after concentrated hydrofluoric acid spilled over his forearm. Irrigation and topical calcium treatment had reduced local pain. During monitored hospital observation he developed hand spasms on both sides and ventricular ectopy; the ECG report described a lengthening QT interval. Serum calcium had fallen below the laboratory reference interval.

cues.why: The key repeats the known injury category while the vascular option belongs to a different service and is directly disfavored by the supplied circulation findings. A reader can choose the burn specialist without interpreting depth.

cues.phrase: The fingers remain warm with brisk nail-bed refill and unchanged Doppler signals.
cues.why: Necessary safety information also disposes of the only competing specialist option; the remaining contrast is specialist versus routine dressings.

review.title: Match procedural burn care to capability

cues.phrase: it has no monitored procedural-sedation service
cues.why: This directly names the capability supplied by the uniquely different option, 'monitored procedural wound care'.

cues.phrase: after the current oral premedication
cues.why: Both distractors repeat the same unsuccessful approach. The key alone introduces a new treatment capability, allowing novelty-based selection.

review.title: Pause feeding for a changed burn trajectory

cues.phrase: Urgent resuscitation and abdominal assessment proceed.

cues.phrase: Pause enteral delivery during reassessment

fairness: Pausing enteral delivery is clearly the best offered prescription during this deterioration. A postpyloric tube does not treat compromised bowel perfusion. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

suggestions: Keep all clinically necessary warning signs. Seek explicit acceptance as a safety exception or revise the scored decision to distinguish credible causes of new feeding intolerance using supported acquired observations.
